response.consequence: On instances without team billing, newly created organizations have a null slug. Org URL and subdomain routing break, and later slug-collision checks cannot match the org. On billing-enabled instances, the slug is claimed before payment or verification.
response.explanation: The old code set `slug` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` and set `metadata.requestedSlug` only when billing was enabled. The change rewrote the first spread as `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, which drops the negation. With billing disabled, which is the self-hosted default, the organization is now created with neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`. With billing enabled, `slug` is set immediately and `requestedSlug` is also set, so the organization is no longer pending approval of the requested slug. This is a behavior change inside a diff that otherwise only changes destinationCalendar to an array.
response.title: Organization slug condition inverted: no slug is stored when team billing is disabled

response.consequence: Creating a booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar (for example, a user with no connected Google Calendar) now fails with a TypeError. Before this change it fell back to Cal Video, so the booking and its event creation break.
response.explanation: destinationCalendar is now an array, and callers pass `[]` when neither the booking nor the user has a destination calendar. In `create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` gives `undefined` for an empty or missing array. The next condition then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was null-safe. So when `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and there is no destination calendar, the property access throws instead of falling back to Cal Video (`integrations:daily`). The `&&` does not guard against this, because the left side is true in exactly that case. I did not read the callers of `create` in the snapshot. The three changed handlers (bookingReminder, confirm, editLocation) do build `[]` for this case.
response.title: EventManager.create throws TypeError for Google Meet when destinationCalendar is empty

response.consequence: The booking is not written to the other collective hosts' calendars. Nothing logs the omission.
response.explanation: evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The new code then runs `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, and the optional chaining skips the push. Calendars collected from the other COLLECTIVE hosts (lines 992-993) are discarded. Example: a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but the second host has one. The team calendars are collected and never used.
response.title: Collective team members' destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none

response.explanation: The class field type now matches CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar (DestinationCalendar[] | null) in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts. The added optional externalId on EventResult is backward compatible.
response.title: No defect found

response.consequence: When a caller omits `externalCalendarId` and the destination calendar is a non-primary calendar, the delete or cancel runs against the user's primary calendar. The event stays in the real destination calendar, or the wrong calendar is touched. Updates in the same situation fail because there is no calendarId.
response.explanation: The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` was empty. The new fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it looks for a calendar whose externalId equals undefined, null or an empty string. That search never finds a real calendar and always returns undefined. In `deleteEvent` the call then uses the "primary" calendar instead of the event's destination calendar. In `updateEvent`, `calendarId` is undefined and the Google API call fails.

other_findings.consequence: Event updates fail whenever `externalCalendarId` is missing. Before this change they used the destination calendar.
other_findings.explanation: The same broken `find` comparison in `updateEvent` always yields undefined when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. `calendar.events.update` is then called with `calendarId: undefined`.
other_findings.title: Google updateEvent has no calendar fallback when externalCalendarId is empty

response.consequence: Calendar events created from Stripe or PayPal payment confirmation get an organizer attendee with id "undefined". PayPal events also lose the organizer's time format. Providers that validate the id may reject the event or store bad data.
response.explanation: The Stripe getBooking, the cron reminder handler and the Stripe handlePaymentSuccess all build `organizer`, but only getBooking and the cron handler set `id`. handlePaymentSuccess in webhook.ts (organizer block, lines 219-225) and the PayPal handlePaymentSuccess (organizer block, lines 144-149) leave it out. The PayPal organizer also omits `timeFormat`. `Person.id` is optional in Calendar.d.ts, so this compiles. GoogleCalendarService spreads the organizer and sets `id: String(calEventRaw.organizer.id)` at lines 119 and 225. With no id that becomes the string "undefined" in the organizer attendee entry. These two handlers are the ones that create the calendar event after payment.
response.title: Payment-success CalendarEvents omit organizer.id, which Google Calendar stringifies

response.consequence: When a caller omits externalCalendarId, the delete targets the user's primary calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar. An event booked on a non-primary calendar is then not deleted; the call fails with 404 or leaves the event in place. If the same uid exists on the primary calendar, that event is deleted instead.
response.explanation: The fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy (undefined, null or ""), but it searches event.destinationCalendar for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value. No real destination calendar has such an externalId, so the fallback always yields undefined and calendarId becomes "primary". The previous code used event.destinationCalendar?.externalId. The change made destinationCalendar an array (Calendar.d.ts:171) but did not write a working lookup, for example the first entry or the one matching the credential. The same pattern is at line 256 in the update path.
response.title: deleteEvent fallback compares against falsy externalCalendarId and never finds a calendar
